title: Bengal Provincial Election and Coalition Ministry
subtitle: Electoral politics under provincial autonomy produced a new coalition-centered power structure in Bengal.
summary: The 1937 provincial election in Bengal, held under the 1935 constitutional framework, produced fragmented outcomes that required coalition bargaining. A. K. Fazlul Huq's ministry emerged through cross-party negotiation rather than single-party dominance. The episode highlighted class, communal, and regional tensions within representative politics and influenced the constitutional path toward the 1940s partition debates.
heroTagline: 1937 showed that constitutional reform could widen representation while intensifying coalition conflict.
whyItMatters: The 1937 election matters because it reveals how electoral design, social blocs, and coalition politics in Bengal shaped the late colonial trajectory toward partition-era realignments.
